title: Budget tool models TOTAL SPEND, not the surplus — the variable estimate is ABS benchmark x household size and neither path ever reads income; Reza's stated rule (budget the remainder in 3 modes) was never captured

plain.issue: The budget tool works out what a household your size typically spends, using national averages, and calls that your budget. It never looks at what you actually have left over. On your numbers: income $41,303 minus committed $14,261 leaves $27,042 a month to budget - and that $27,042 is the number the three options should be splitting up.

notes: Auto-raised by issues:raise (NeoAudit finding bus, §3.1). Surface: lib/budget-analysis/aiPrompt.ts:311. Expected: remainder = monthly net income - committed; the tool offers three modes of allocating THAT remainder (Reza's stated product rule). Actual: calculateBenchmarkExpenses(params, trackedCategories) takes only {adultsCount, childrenCount, childrenAges, petsCount, petTypes, carsCount, lifestylePreference} - income is not in scope. Every category is headcount x ABS 2023-24 base rate x lifestyle multiplier. Income enters route.ts ONLY at :262-269/:284-286/:390/:551 as a post-hoc exceeds-income flag, never as an input. Scenarios (:381-383) are Minimum/Recommended/Comfortable modes of TOTAL SPEND.. Evidence/run: VR-041. Unmodelled semanticKey(s) — MODEL then attach (§21.5): monthlyInflow.

title: aggregateIncome has NO one-off gate and 'net' is only net for SALARY — quickMetrics.monthlyIncome reads $41,303/mo ($495,636/yr) labelled net-of-PAYG against the app's own declared GROSS of $317,751/yr

plain.issue: Your monthly income shows as $41,303 in the budget tool and on the year-to-date chart. That is $495,636 a year, described as after-tax — but the Tax page says you earned $317,751 before tax. After-tax income cannot be larger than before-tax income. The Income page separately says $25,335 a month.

notes: Auto-raised by issues:raise (NeoAudit finding bus, §3.1). Surface: lib/calculations/incomeAggregator.ts:160. Expected: net monthly income <= gross monthly income ($317,751/12 = $26,479); one-off income rows contribute 0 to a monthly run-rate; one centralised income figure per the quickMetrics SSOT contract at masterFinancialService.ts:350-352. Actual: quickMetrics.monthlyIncome = $41,303/mo = $495,636/yr, 56% ABOVE declared gross and labelled 'monthly NET income (after PAYG)'. The Income page states a different net monthly ($25,335) and the Activity YTD Sankey shares this producer ($496K/yr).. Evidence/run: VR-041. Unmodelled semanticKey(s) — MODEL then attach (§21.5): monthlyInflow. | VR-041, TRACED END-TO-END. CHAIN: masterFinancialService.ts:2100 quickMetrics.monthlyIncome = monthlyIncome.all.netTotal <- :1865 buildIncomeBreakdown(...) <- :1130 aggregateIncome(aggregateSource) <- lib/calculations/incomeAggregator.ts:160 loop. THREE defects found in that loop: (1) NO ONE-OFF GATE - grep for isRecurring/monthlyRunRate/oneOff in incomeAggregator.ts returns NOTHING. getNetAmount:106 does converter(item.amount, item.frequency) raw, so every one-off income row is annualised as if it recurs. This is the MON-053 defect (one-off ATO deposits annualised x12) fixed on the TAX path but never on this aggregate, and the exact income-side twin of MON-125/MON-126. (2) 'NET' IS ONLY NET FOR SALARY - :105-106 comments 'For non-salary income, we don't deduct tax', so rental and other income flow through GROSS while the field is typed and consumed as 'monthly NET income (after PAYG)' (:354). (3) NOT ESTABLISHED, flag only: :96-98 returns item.netAmount/12 for SALARY+GROSS regardless of item.frequency, assuming netAmount is annual. Whether any row stores it otherwise was NOT traced. EXPECTATION FROM ARITHMETIC LAW: net income cannot exceed gross income. Declared gross is $317,751/yr = $26,479/mo (Tax page, VR-041). Net-of-tax is approximately 317,751 - 37,786 = $279,965/yr = $23,330/mo, consistent with the Income page's own $25,335. The reported $41,303/mo is ~77% above that and definitionally impossible. BLAST RADIUS: this value feeds savingsRate (:1413), debtToIncome (:1422), the MON-125 budget income-sanity guard (app/api/budget-analysis/generate/route.ts:267) and the health score - so the -30.5% savings rate, the 416% debt-to-income and the budget guard are all computed on it. SSOT NOTE: masterFinancialService.ts:350-352 states the contract explicitly - 'any surface that wants the 3-line personal-P&L scoreboard reads from here, never re-derives' - yet the Income page shows $25,335 and Home's KPI shows $19,899/mo. This is the unlabelled fourth basis recorded in VR-040 as MON-059, now identified as this producer.

Twelve different parts of the app treat them as costing nothing, because they read the contractual minimum repayment — which is zero for an interest-only loan. notes: Auto-raised by issues:raise (NeoAudit finding bus, §3.1). Surface: lib/services/moneyFlowService.ts:385. Expected: every per-loan monthly cost comes from resolveLoanMonthlyCost() / totalLoanMonthlyCost() (actuals -> contractual minRepayment -> interest floor), per MON-081 and the #1523 migration. title: Reference Numbers — every canonical financial quantity has multiple producers (~336 across 23 quantities); one calc engine per named number, enforced

plain.issue: Every important number in Monitrax is worked out in many different places, each with its own formula — spending 28 ways, cashflow 27, depreciation 22, PAYG 23. That is why the same figure disagrees between screens: there is no single answer to compare against, so fixing one place never fixes the number. Only the Medicare levy is calculated in exactly one place.

title: Emergency fund must be a SURVIVAL RUNWAY — liquid cash / (essential expenses - salary-independent income), answering 'if I lose my salary, how long do I last' (Reza decision 2026-07-29)

plain.issue: Your Safety Net says 11.6 months, worked out as your cash divided by everything you spend. That is not what an emergency fund is for. It should answer one question: if your salary stopped tomorrow, how long could you last - which means subtracting the income that keeps arriving anyway, like your rent.

notes: Auto-raised by issues:raise (NeoAudit finding bus, §3.1). Surface: lib/services/masterFinancialService.ts:1384. Expected: liquid cash / (essential expenses - salary-independent 'safe' income such as rental), with the sentence 'if you lose your salary income, how long you can survive' shown on the page. Actual: Safety Net divides liquid cash by TOTAL monthly outgoings ($25,973/mo incl. one-off capital spend) giving 11.6 months. Three producers disagree on the denominator: masterFinancialService:1384 uses actual average outflow, scoreCalculator:190 uses essential-only, metricAggregation:163 uses all declared expenses and counts shares/ETFs as liquid.. Evidence/run: VR-041. Unmodelled semanticKey(s) — MODEL then attach (§21.5): monthlyOutflow. | REZA DECISION 2026-07-29, this is the SPEC not an option: the emergency fund is a SURVIVAL RUNWAY. FORMULA: liquid cash / (essential expenses - salary-independent 'safe' income such as rental). The sentence 'if you lose your salary income, how long you can survive' MUST APPEAR ON THE PAGE - the label is part of the fix, not decoration. INDICATIVE ONLY at f13368ef, pending MON-128: liquid $301,808; committed $14,261/mo (recurring essentials $1,482 + canonical loans $12,779); rental ~$10,102/mo; net burn ~$4,159/mo; runway ~72 months against the 11.6 shown today. DO NOT BUILD ON THESE INPUTS YET - the rental figure is itself unresolved (Income page $121,227/yr vs Tax page $121,881/yr) and every income aggregate is suspect until MON-128 lands. SUB-DECISION RESOLVED (Reza, 2026-07-29): LOAN REPAYMENTS ARE ESSENTIAL. essential = recurring bills + all loan repayments = $1,482 + $12,779 = $14,261/mo. Rationale: the bank still wants paying if salary stops. Net burn = 14,261 - rental ~10,102 = ~$4,159/mo; runway ~72 months on liquid $301,808. SPEC IS NOW COMPLETE - build once MON-128 has made the income inputs trustworthy.
